messages.subject: too many low abundance bugs
parts:
Hi,
I posted the following question over two weeks ago with no reply. So I try again. I would like to run Maaslin on functional (KEGG) data. I tried in R with this:
Maaslin("patients.tsv", "/Users/stepra/Results/Maaslin/output1", iLastMetadata=5)
but get the following warnings for all samples:
2018-05-02 12:39:22 INFO:maaslin:Running quality control.
2018-05-02 12:39:22 INFO:maaslin:Removing the following for too many low abundance bugs.
2018-05-02 12:39:22 INFO:maaslin:P_19
 2018-05-02 12:39:22 INFO:maaslin:P_25
 2018-05-02 12:39:22 INFO:maaslin:P_25.1
 2018-05-02 12:39:22 INFO:maaslin:P_34
 2018-05-02 12:39:22 INFO:maaslin:P_36
 2018-05-02 12:39:22 INFO:maaslin:P_08
 2018-05-02 12:39:22 INFO:maaslin:P_34.1
 2018-05-02 12:39:22 INFO:maaslin:P_28
 2018-05-02 12:39:22 INFO:maaslin:P_15
 2018-05-02 12:39:22 INFO:maaslin:P_04
 2018-05-02 12:39:22 INFO:maaslin:P_20
 
the values are sometimes below 1 but not extremely low and the sums are 600-800 for 170 rows. So how can I solve this?
Thanks a lot for your help!
Stef

messages.author: 3bf2dfbdb300e013
messages.subject: Re: too many low abundance bugs
parts:
Hi Stef,

MaAsLin requires the data to be proportional between 0 and 1 for the default linear modeling. If your data is not proportional (which seems to be true in your case), you can still run MaAsLin without worries by specifying strTransform='none', as the default arc-sine square root transformation is not valid for non-proportional values. A similar argument also applies to the default filtering (dMinAbd = 0.0001, dMinSamp = 0.1), which is more appropriate for proportional relative abundance data. You can tune these two parameters according to your filtering need, which should take care of the warnings you are seeing, in addition to ensuring a valid analysis. Let me know if that answers your question.

Many thanks,
Himel

messages.author: 3bf2dfbdb300e013
messages.subject: Re: too many low abundance bugs
parts:
Hi Stef,

In your attached metaphlan2 file, the relative abundances are percentages (between 0 and 100), which you need to convert to proportions (between 0 and 1) prior to running MaAsLin. Also, following up on your last email, I had the impression that you were getting some warnings but those were not necessarily errors. As mentioned in the previous email, you can always tune the parameters dMinAbd and dMinSamp to suppress the warnings. But, other than that, warnings can be ignored in most cases.

Many thanks,
Himel
